titleEn: When the Bridge Lantern Glows, Off to Sleep!

pages.text: "I don't want to sleep yet! I want to find more shells!" Pongi splashed her paws in the water beneath the bridge. The sky was growing dark. She could still see shells, so she held back a yawn.
Grandpa Goose, the canal keeper in boots, lit the bridge lantern. Pop! One lantern shone in the dark night. Dad, in his overalls, said, "Pongi, the lantern is lit. It's bedtime."

"I'm not sleepy at all!" Pongi shook her head. But her eyelids grew heavy. Her splashing paws stopped in midair, and water dripped from their tips. Her mouth opened in a big yawn. "Oh? Maybe I really am sleepy..."
Dad scooped Pongi up and carried her home along the bank. "Let's get ready for bed while we watch the lantern." Dad sang softly, "When the bridge lantern glows, off to sleep!"
They got ready one step at a time. First, brush your teeth! At the water tub by the doorway, Pongi brushed and brushed. Bubbles foamed up. Dad brushed beside her too.

Second, blow out the house lantern! Pongi blew it out, then thumped her tail on the floor. The room went dark. But the bridge lantern shone through one window. It wasn't scary, because Grandpa's lantern was there.
Third, under the blanket! Pongi pulled the blanket over herself on the sofa by the window. Dad bent down, kissed her forehead, and sang, "When the bridge lantern glows, off to sleep!"
Pongi looked at the bridge lantern through the window and whispered, "Grandpa, thank you for the lantern. I'm going to sleep now." Then her eyes slowly closed.

Under her blanket, Pongi counted the steps. "One, stop playing when the lantern lights up! Two, brush your teeth! Three, blow out the lantern and sleep under the blanket!" Her voice grew softer, until only gentle breathing could be heard.

Toot! The first boat went past, and the window was bright. Dad gently hugged Pongi. "A good sleep made you strong again, didn't it?" "When the bridge lantern glows, off to sleep! I'll sleep tonight too!" Pongi stretched.
